35/G.goal: Explain how usability requirements for an interactive system are gathered and specified by placing requirement gathering in the interactive system development lifecycle, applying user-centered design, and using contextual inquiry to derive requirements from specified users and contexts.
35/G.achieves: Prepares the learner to conduct usability requirement gathering and specification in the course's XR system development case study, giving a user-centered starting point for later system design and implementation.

35/O1.goal: Explain how requirement gathering frames end-user usability requirements in interactive system development by contrasting user-centered and system-centered design and by identifying usability requirements as non-functional interface-quality requirements rather than feasibility, interface, or code design decisions.
35/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a user-centered basis for specifying what usability must be required before designing an interactive or XR system, supporting the requirement-gathering stage of the course's system development case study.

35/O2.goal: Describe how contextual inquiry is used to gather usability requirements by observing specified users in a specified context of use and tracing observed user activities to essential system features.
35/O2.achieves: Enables the learner to elicit real usability requirements from users and their work context, so that XR system features and design decisions are grounded in actual user needs rather than assumptions.
